findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key you were issued. Append it as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Query parameter api_key is rejected with HTTP 401 ('send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'). Key must be in the X-API-Key header.
findings.how_found: Sent requests with ?api_key= query parameter and inspected the 401 response message.
findings.impact: All API requests fail authentication if following documented query parameter approach.

findings.documented: Response 200 returns 'token', 'token_type': 'Bearer', 'expires_in': 86400 (24 hours), 'user': {'email': '...', 'name': 'Demo User'}. There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Returns 'access_token' (not 'token'), 'refresh_token', 'expires_in': 900 (15 minutes), and 'refresh_url': '/auth/refresh'. The user object does not include 'name'.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/login with valid demo credentials and inspected JSON response.
findings.impact: Clients expecting 'token' fail to read auth bearer token, and sessions terminate after 15 minutes unless refreshed.

findings.documented: Tokens are valid for 24 hours... There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts {'refresh_token': '...'} along with X-API-Key to issue a fresh access_token and refresh_token.
findings.how_found: Observed refresh_url in login response and executed POST /auth/refresh successfully.
findings.impact: Allows client sessions to stay active seamlessly past the 15-minute access token lifespan without requiring re-login.

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Returns HTTP 200 with {'ok': true, 'note': 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side'}. Tokens are stateless JWTs and not invalidated server-side.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout and tested subsequent requests using the logged-out token; tokens remain valid until expiration.
findings.impact: Server-side invalidation is not performed; client application must explicitly clear stored tokens.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page (1-indexed, default 1) and limit (default 20, max 200). Collection responses are shaped: {'total': 1240, 'page': 1, 'page_size': 20, 'results': [...]}.
findings.actual: Parameter 'page' is quietly ignored; pagination uses 'offset' (0-indexed). Parameter 'limit' is capped at 50 (requesting 200 returns 50). Response contains 'limit', 'offset', 'count', 'total', 'has_more', 'results', omitting 'page' and 'page_size'.
findings.how_found: Queried collection endpoints with different combinations of page, offset, and limit and inspected response schema and returned records.
findings.impact: Requesting page=2 returns page 1 endlessly; limit requests above 50 fail to return more than 50 items.

findings.documented: 'total' is the exact number of records matching your filters. To fetch every record, read total, divide by your limit, and request that many pages.
findings.actual: Response 'total' reports 4348, but the endpoint actually serves 4700 records with 'has_more: true' continuing up to offset 4700.
findings.how_found: Paged through /v1/listings following has_more until false, retrieving 4700 total records.
findings.impact: Clients calculating page counts from 'total' miss 352 listings.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns both active and inactive records: 978 records out of 4700 have 'is_live: false'.
findings.how_found: Analyzed is_live boolean distribution across all retrieved listings.
findings.impact: Inactive and withdrawn properties are exposed to users unless filtered client-side.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Multiple listing records describe the exact same physical property cross-posted on multiple portals by different brokers with identical building, floor, BHK, bathrooms, and facing direction.
findings.how_found: Deduplicated listings by physical property attributes (locality, apartment_name, floor, total_floors, bedroom, bathroom, facing_direction), identifying 117 duplicate property pairs (234 records).
findings.impact: Users see identical properties repeated across browse results.

findings.documented: Listing records contain valid physical real estate data.
findings.actual: 32 listing records contain physically impossible data: 8 records with floor > total_floors, 8 with carpet_area > super_built_up_area, 8 with negative prices, and 8 with latitude and longitude swapped.
findings.how_found: Executed domain constraint validation scripts across all 4700 listing records.
findings.impact: Causes UI anomalies such as negative pricing, impossible floor ratios, and map pins placed in oceans or alternate hemispheres.

findings.documented: Returns genuine sale listings with market pricing in rupees.
findings.actual: 8 listings feature fake enquiry-bait prices under ₹17,000 (ranging between ₹6,250 and ₹16,790) for full sale apartments to attract leads.
findings.how_found: Performed distribution analysis of price and price-per-square-foot ratios, uncovering a distinct cluster under ₹17,000 separated from the rest of the market (which starts at ₹2.17M).
findings.impact: Misleads buyers with fake price bait and heavily distorts pricing analytics.

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Listings from magichomes (website == 'magichomes') report carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square meters (sqm) rather than square feet (values between 35 and 200 for 1-4 BHK units).
findings.how_found: Computed carpet area distributions grouped by website and observed that MagicHomes values were ~10.76x smaller.
findings.impact: Price per square foot calculations and area filtering produce errors unless converted using the 10.7639 multiplier.

findings.documented: Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: The 'posted_at' timestamps in /v1/listings omit the 'Z' UTC suffix and timezone offsets, returning naive local datetime strings in IST (e.g. '2026-06-29T07:02:00').
findings.how_found: Inspected all posted_at strings in /v1/listings; none contained 'Z' or timezone offsets.
findings.impact: Standard ISO 8601 parsers may misinterpret timestamps as local browser time, resulting in offset errors.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} - A single listing.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{id} returns HTTP 404 Not Found. The endpoint exists at the plural path GET /v1/listings/{id}.
findings.how_found: Called /v1/listing/100-1000461 (returned 404) and verified /v1/listings/100-1000461 returns 200.
findings.impact: Single listing detail pages fail to load if using the documented singular path.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar - Up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{id}/similar returns HTTP 404 Not Found for all listings.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings/{id}/similar with valid listing IDs.
findings.impact: Similar property recommendations fail on backend and must be calculated client-side.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body {'id': '...'}, DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites routes return HTTP 404 Not Found. The working endpoint is /v1/saved, and POST /v1/saved requires body {'listing_id': '...'} rather than {'id': '...'}.
findings.how_found: Probed /v1/favourites (all 404), discovered /v1/saved, and verified POST/DELETE behavior.
findings.impact: Favourites/saved properties fail completely unless using /v1/saved with listing_id.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary - Pre-computed aggregates for your city.
findings.actual: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.how_found: Sent GET request to /v1/analytics/summary; received 404.
findings.impact: Analytics dashboards cannot rely on server precomputations and must compute metrics from raw data.

findings.documented: Money: Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API. price_min and price_max are in rupees.
findings.actual: In /v1/projects, price_min and price_max are floats denominated in Crores (for values < 10) or Lakhs (for values >= 10), not integer rupees.
findings.how_found: Inspected all 520 project records; price_min and price_max values range from 1.0 to 99.8.
findings.impact: Projects display prices like ₹2 instead of ₹2 Crores unless normalized.

findings.documented: 'total_listings' is the number of listings currently available in the project. It is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: 'total_listings' is incorrect for 127 projects compared to active listings. Additionally, GET /v1/listings?project_id=... quietly ignores the project_id filter and returns unfiltered listings.
findings.how_found: Counted active listings per project_id and identified 127 mismatches; queried GET /v1/listings?project_id=P10001 and observed unfiltered results.
findings.impact: Users see incorrect project listing counts, and filtering listings by project fails server-side.

findings.documented: Endpoint is not present in documentation.
findings.actual: GET /v1/me returns user context, city_id: 1, city: 'bangalore', assigned_locality: 'whitefield', and reference_date: '2026-09-10T00:00:00+05:30'.
findings.how_found: Probed /v1/me with bearer token and X-API-Key header.
findings.impact: Provides programmatic access to assigned locality and city metadata.

findings.documented: Endpoint is not present in documentation.
findings.actual: GET /v1/localities returns city name ('bangalore'), locality count (10), and array of localities with listing counts summing exactly to 4700.
findings.how_found: Probed /v1/localities with authenticated session.
findings.impact: Enables instant locality filtering and aggregate counts without fetching all listings.
